headline: Will I love again?
note:
🔄 REWRITTEN 2026-08-19 to the Natural Tarot-Cut framework. Bubbles 3-6 run as ONE causal chain — so / and / but / that's why. This is a SELF-FRAME hook, so the hopeful yes is affirmed with certainty; the DATE stays banned. The art line and the bridge are unchanged.

Face-UP decks only — arcana-mfh (Magician/Hanged Man/Fool) and arcana-eef (Emperor/Empress/Fool), so she CHOSE the card rather than turned it, and two card-sets means two sets of copy. The Fool copy is shared between them, verb already correct.

⭐ THESE ARE THE ONLY TWO HOOKS ON THE FUNNEL THAT READ HER RATHER THAN HIM. SELF_FRAME_HOOKS swaps 'tendency, never a verdict' for 'affirm the hopeful yes with certainty' — which is safe here precisely because no specific man exists to be convicted or acquitted. So these are warmer than everything else in this batch, on purpose.

⚠️ SEED FAMILY WITH NO GUARD FILE (`tests/tarot-self-frame-copy.test.ts` does not exist) — only the generic guards apply. 🔴 Still never tie it to one named person and 🔴 never give a date. cards-soulmate's tendency permits the 'when' to be answered only as a LEANING, never as a timeframe.

Finding: she is not really asking about a future person — she is asking whether the part of her that loves has been used up. It has not, and this is one of the few landers on the funnel allowed to say so plainly.

a: You chose the Magician, dear. Look — the roses over his head are fully out.
You asked if you'll love again. Your hand went to the man who can still make things.
So yes, dear. The part of you that loves isn't used up.
And the roses are out again, dear. They come back every winter.
But you've been told otherwise, dear. I don't think that was true.
That's why you look yourself over for damage, dear. There's none to find.
Let me look closer at what has been sitting over that part of you…
b: You chose the Hanged Man, dear. Look — the gold at his head is the brightest thing on the card.
You asked if you'll love again. Your hand went to the card that pauses before a turn.
So you've been in a pause, dear. Not an ending.
And the gold is brightest at the very point of hanging, dear.
But something in you kept its light through all of it, dear.
That's why things can still move you, dear. It is all intact.
Let me look closer at what has been dimming it from outside…
c: You chose the Fool, dear. Look — the flower in his hand is fresh and white.
You asked if you'll love again. Your hand went to the one who begins again.
So beginning again is the whole of this card, dear.
And the flower is fresh, dear, and he carries it forward with him.
But you've been told you carry a dead thing, dear. You carry that.
That's why it feels so heavy, dear. You've held it up alone.
Let me look closer at what has been weighing on your hands…

a: You chose the Emperor, dear. Look — his beard is long and white and reaches his chest.
You asked if you'll love again. Your hand went to the man who has seen a great deal.
So you've come a long way, dear. It shows, and it should.
And he's old and seated, dear, and still holding the whole thing up.
But a long past doesn't use a person up, dear.
That's why the years have felt like a loss, dear. They never were.
Let me look closer at what has been taking from that count…
b: You chose the Empress, dear. Look — the trees behind her are dark green and close together.
You asked if you'll love again. Your hand went to the card of things that grow back.
So things grow back, dear. That is what she is.
And the trees behind her are thick, dear, and none of it was forced.
But you don't have to make it happen by trying, dear.
That's why the trying has worn you out, dear. It was never the problem.
Let me look closer at what has been shading this over…
c: You chose the Fool, dear. Look — the flower in his hand is fresh and white.
You asked if you'll love again. Your hand went to the one who begins again.
So beginning again is the whole of this card, dear.
And the flower is fresh, dear, and he carries it forward with him.
But you've been told you carry a dead thing, dear. You carry that.
That's why it feels so heavy, dear. You've held it up alone.
Let me look closer at what has been weighing on your hands…
